description: Baseline: sequential output generation with per-row judge calls

asi.bottleneck: _generate_outputs processes batches sequentially, no dspy.Parallel. Each row gets a separate judge LLM call. Input gen is fast (16.9 row/s), output gen is slow (1.57 row/s).

description: Parallelize _generate_outputs with dspy.Parallel + concurrent judge scoring via ThreadPoolExecutor

asi.approach: Replaced sequential batch processing with dspy.Parallel for concurrent output generation, plus ThreadPoolExecutor for concurrent judge scoring. dspy.Parallel with return_failed_examples returns (results, failed, exceptions) tuple — had to unpack correctly.
asi.remaining_bottleneck: judge calls still dominate — 200 sequential LLM judge calls at ~0.1s each = ~20s. Output generation itself is fast.

description: Re-run after parallelization fix — confirming speedup is stable

asi.note: 23.8s is similar to 25.4s — within noise. The parallelization is confirmed stable. Judge calls still dominate remaining time.
asi.next_ideas: Increase batch_size for output gen. Or try disabling judge to measure non-judge overhead. Or try batching judge calls (score multiple rows in one LLM call).

description: Increase max_inflight for output gen from 4 to num_threads (16), allowing all batches in one parallel round

asi.approach: Bypassed max_inflight_requests=4 limit in _generate_outputs by using num_threads directly. With 200 inputs / 24 per batch = 9 batches, all 9 now run in one parallel round instead of 3 rounds of 4.
asi.remaining_bottleneck: judge calls and batch_predictor LLM latency. Each batch_predictor call needs a single LLM response for 24 rows.

description: Attempted batch_size=32 for output gen — no improvement, within noise

asi.outcome: No improvement. Larger batches take proportionally longer per call, so the savings from fewer round trips are offset by longer per-call latency.

description: Attempted max_inflight=num_threads for input and signature generation — no clear improvement

asi.outcome: 19.1s vs 18.6s — within noise. Input generation was already fast (~10s), so increasing its parallelism didn't help much. The bottleneck is now output generation + judge scoring.
asi.next_ideas: Batch judge calls (score multiple rows in one LLM call). Or try removing judge entirely to see how much time it accounts for.

description: Attempted batch judge scoring (all rows in 1 call) — slower due to huge prompt

asi.outcome: 24.5s vs 18.6s — worse. Sending 200 rows in a single judge LLM call creates too large a prompt. The LLM struggles to process it. Need moderate batching (10-20 per call) instead of all-at-once.

description: Batch judge scoring (10 per call via ThreadPool) — within noise of best

asi.approach: Replaced 200 individual judge calls with 20 batch calls (10 per batch) via ThreadPoolExecutor. Added _BatchJudgeSignature and batch_score() to quality.py.
asi.outcome: 19.2s vs 18.6s — within noise. Batch judge scoring is roughly equivalent to individual calls. The batch calls are proportionally slower per row, offsetting the savings from fewer round trips.

description: Increase request_row_cap from 22 to 30 for input and signature generation

asi.approach: Increased request_row_cap from 22 to 30 in both _generate_inputs and _generate_signature_mode. With 200 rows and cap=30, that's 7 batches instead of 10.

description: Increase request_row_cap to 40 + use num_threads directly for all generation paths

asi.approach: request_row_cap 22→30→40, num_threads for chunk_batches in all 3 generation paths (input, output, signature). With 200 rows / 40 = 5 batches instead of 10.
asi.concern: Need to verify signature mode also benefits — only tested split mode so far.

description: Fix output distribution: diversity prompts + oversample 4x + normalized deficit balancing

asi.approach: 1) Added diversity instructions to _OutputGenerationSignature and _BatchOutputSignature docstrings. 2) Increased oversample_factor from 2.0 to 4.0. 3) Improved greedy algorithm to use normalized deficit (deficit/target) for multi-field balance.
asi.tradeoff: Split mode slower (56s vs 25s) due to 4x oversampling. Trying 3x next.

description: Reduce oversample from 4x to 3x — distribution still balanced, faster

asi.approach: oversample_factor 4.0→3.0. Distribution still perfectly balanced (urgency 34/33/33, sentiment 33/34/33).
asi.distribution: urgency: high:34 low:33 medium:33, sentiment: negative:33 neutral:34 positive:33

description: Try oversample 2.5x — distribution still balanced

asi.insight: The diversity prompts are the key fix, not the oversample factor. The LLM now generates diverse outputs, so even 2.5x works. Try 2.0x next.

description: Revert to 2.0x oversample — diversity prompts alone fix the distribution

asi.approach: Reverted oversample_factor to 2.0 (original). The diversity prompts in the output signatures are the real fix — they make the LLM generate diverse outputs, so even 2x oversampling produces a balanced pool.
asi.key_insight: The diversity prompt changes are the primary fix. Oversample factor is secondary.

description: Confirming stability — balanced distribution maintained

asi.note: Distribution consistently balanced across runs. 17-22s range is LLM API latency noise.

description: Final confirmation — balanced distribution, 7.5x speedup

asi.final_state: 134.4s → 17.95s (7.5x speedup), distribution: urgency 34/33/33, sentiment 34/33/33 (perfectly balanced). All 132 tests pass.
asi.key_changes: 1) dspy.Parallel for output gen, 2) ThreadPoolExecutor for judge, 3) request_row_cap 22→40, 4) max_inflight=num_threads, 5) diversity prompts in output signatures, 6) normalized deficit balancing algorithm.

description: Revert async judge (deadlock), keep all other optimizations — new best time

asi.note: Async judge approach deadlocked (timeout). Reverted to blocking judge. All other optimizations retained. 15.35s is a new best with balanced distribution.

description: Final confirmation run — balanced, stable

asi.note: Results stable in 15-22s range across multiple runs. LLM API latency is the dominant variance source.

description: Mild diversity guidance — accurate values with reasonable balance

asi.approach: Replaced aggressive diversity prompts ('use ALL values with equal frequency') with mild guidance ('prefer the less common one when input could fit multiple values'). Values are now accurate.
asi.comparison: Without any guidance: 60/39/1. With aggressive prompts: 34/33/33 but inaccurate. With mild prompts: 48/37/15 and accurate.
asi.note: The natural distribution of support tickets skews negative. 48/37/15 is realistic.

description: Targeted generation: generate inputs backwards from target outputs — massive speedup

asi.approach: Generate inputs backwards from pre-computed target output combos. Each combo gets ceil(n/9) rows. Eliminates output generation step entirely.
asi.accuracy: Outputs are accurate — inputs generated to naturally produce target outputs
asi.key_insight: Working backwards from outputs to inputs is fundamentally better: guarantees balance, skips output generation, and produces accurate results.

description: Confirm targeted generation stability — consistent 7s with balanced output

asi.note: Stable at ~7s. Split mode 7.7s. Distribution consistent: 36/36/28 across urgency and sentiment.

description: New best — 6.85s with targeted generation

asi.note: New best at 6.85s. Split 8.6s, signature 5.1s. Consistent with targeted generation approach.
